A strong entry, I really enjoy compact and easy to understand articles such as this. The twist at the end really does it for me, and I personally feel you don't need to give any more detail on what happened to Mr. Kepler's family as it leaves me wondering.

However, a few of the emails feel quite pointless, when they could instead be changed in a way that is relevant to the narrative to keep up the flow. The dialouge did also feel quite stiff in places, bodering on an unnatural zone between formal business and informal banter.

item.content:encoded:
After reading this article, I have to say it was good overall. The pacing was pretty good in the gradual process of the product's cycle, from being created to it's effects and the aftermath of Kepler's situation.

Critique:
I liked the banter between Brain and Lana, though the dialogue at the beginning with seemed a bit unnatural, but nothing too out of the ordinary. Also, I wish there was a bit more to the situation with Kepler's wife and son, mostly in just giving a bit more detail as to what happened concerning their heritage, but not too much to give everything away to the reader.

An enjoyable read. I also liked the disclaimer used for the product. Something very apt for the company to put on one of their products.

+1

item.content:encoded:
My favorite thing about this article is what a lot of others mentioned, and MC&D *didn't* drain Brian to death for short term profit. Silly to either destroy your means of production for a little extra money now, or make everyone terrified to work for you on the thought that they'll end up soul drained as soon as they're not at the top of the game. As well as the implication that at least some of the decision makers care about the morality of their products.

Nice in general to see a side of MC&D that isn't just wildly evil for the hell of it.

item.content:encoded:
I don't feel like this article has a really gripping "hook". Yes, I did figure out what Kepler did with his family, but I just feel like it can be dumbed down to " ambitious technology is misused by a homicidal prick", which reminds me of Black Mirror. The concept itself is interesting, and I found the idea of MC&D enabling anomaly scientists and using their products for profit to be entertaining.
Novoting, as I have kind of mixed feelings about the article as a whole. I would've upvoted if you added a larger variety of fuckups with the product to keep things interesting, since this final version kind of leaves me wanting more.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The setup and fun of the article are well done - this is MC&D the honest business, not the schemers, and it's nice to see that for once.

The middle section of the article leaves something to be desired, however. In particular, it depends on the phrase "shares the same recent heritage as the activator". What that sounds like to me is the same ancestry, which doesn't line up with the rest of the article - in particular, this shouldn't work at all on a spouse, making it strange that the ad just talks about "family members". Maybe that's what the bit about the cute salesperson is refering to, but that doesn't seem like the sort of thing that it's worth lying about.

The final twist depends on the ability for one person to activate the portal and choose its destination, and a different person to go through that portal. The initial description of the portal very much made it sound like the portal was automatically used by the person who activated it. Due to the fact that the twist reveal was quite subtle, this made it easy to miss the twist altogether - I had to go back to reread it.

Overall, I like this piece, but it could use some language changes to make things clearer and therefore hit harder.

item.content:encoded:
I thought the article was decent, if a little straightforward at times. For the most part, I had no issues with it, but I did had a few thoughts(keep in mind that I am not the most experienced writer, and as such my critique should probably be taken with a grain of salt):

+ Warning: spoilers(and thoughts) ahead
- Hide

Most of my problems with the article are with two sentences.

The first one:

"Item will open a single use portal to a location that matches the location the user considers ideal for vacationing."

Considering that a lot of the horror from the twist comes from all the possible ways that Kepler could have "disposed" of his wife and son, I think it should be made more clear that the client can choose the destination. Specifically, the use of the word "ideal" muddies the meaning a bit, and the sentence seems overly clunky(I didn't realize that the customer gets to choose the destination until the I got to the advertisement). Something closer to: "Item will open a single use portal to a chosen vacationing destination." may convey the point more effectively.
Furthermore, the destination being(possibly) anomalous should probably be mentioned(also didn't get this until the advertisement stated it).

And the second:

"We will probably no longer sell the single user versions that let you send people where you want them to go."

This implies that either the family version doesn't allow you to choose the location, which (I think) is not the intended message, or there are versions that let one person send another person where they would like to go, which I don't believe were previously stated to exist.
This could probably be solved by editing Incident Report 13 to state that the special request is for a portal that can let you send people where you want them to go. Depending on how it is executed, it could also be an opportunity to better setup the twist. For example, the reader could be confused/intrigued with the purpose of the special request by making the requested changes generally fairly minor and pointless. Kepler requesting the ability to set the location before use(so that he doesn't have to be in the room when it turns on), and a delay in its activation(so that he can place it in a room with his wife and son, and then leave before it activates), could both serve this purpose. To further play up the oddness of the request(and to keep in the nature of MC&D), Kepler could be said to have been haggled up to exorbitant price in the Incident Report 13.

Overall: Solid article, and, (concurring with LordMetalton and DrArmstrong) nice twist. +1
